archetype: global macro pessimist; markets underprice late-cycle housing, labor and policy-error fragility

conflict_synopsis.core_view: AONIA still prices 51-60bp of extra RBA hikes into a housing and labor downturn that is already in the hard data; receive AU front-end duration as the defensive unwind of that policy-error path.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: October AONIA/RBA window plus the next Australian housing and labor prints testing the residual +21.5 to +51bp hike strip.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AONIA Oct-26 4.565 and Mar-27 4.86 hold or reprice higher while housing/labor stabilize or trimmed-mean CPI re-accelerates from 3.6%.

paper_capital.rationale: The seat already pays 5% ACT/365 on the full $100m whether flat or not, so a defined-invalidation duration long is required whenever the packet shows a path-versus-housing discrepancy. $12m is 12% of allocation: enough for a 20-40bp AONIA/2Y unwind to matter, small enough that the 2022-01 / 2025-12 continuation analogs (further yield selloff) do not dominate NAV. AU 2Y yield 4.999 roughly matches the 5% vig, so the edge is path-repricing, not carry. No mark is invented; if the book engine cannot represent AU_2Y from this packet the parent should record execution_blocked and HOLD.

remit: strongest defensive, slowdown, stress or risk-off macro expression
stance_summary: FACT: Australian housing is already contracting (NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y, volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak) while AONIA still prices +21.5bp by Oct-26, +37.5bp by Dec-26, +51bp by Mar-27 (4.86) and a mid-2027 peak near +59.5bp (4.945) versus overnight AONIA 4.35. FACT: AU 2Y is 4.999, 99.0th percentile 1y. INFERENCE: that residual hike path is a policy error into an unfolding housing/labor downturn and will be aborted or reversed; long AU front-end duration is the cleanest defensive expression of that miss. UNKNOWN: whether sticky trimmed-mean CPI at 3.6% and the global Fed/BoJ tightening wave keep the RBA hiking anyway.

catalysts: Next RBA decision / Oct-26 AONIA expiry as the first 21.5bp of priced hikes is tested.
Further NSW/Australia housing finance, prices or stamp-duty prints confirming the 16 Sep downturn.
AU labor (employment/unemployment/WPI) following through on July's -15.8k / 4.5% loosening.
Global risk-off from Fed/BoJ/energy that forces a broader duration bid and makes the extra AU hikes politically and economically undeliverable.

context_build.causal_mechanism: RBA cash-rate tightening transmits first through housing turnover, collateral values and household cash-flow. NSW stamp-duty and volumes have already collapsed and AU labor/sentiment are softening, so additional priced hikes (Oct-26 through mid-2027) either do not occur or are reversed once the downturn is undeniable. Long AU 2Y / received AONIA profits when that residual path is unwound. This is a domestic slowdown/policy-error mechanism, not a call that every risky currency must fall.

These extremes are discovery signals that a lot of tightening is already in the price, not the thesis.
historical_reference.regime_differences: Three of four same-move AU 2Y analogs saw further yield increases; only 2022-09-28 rallied. Today's 2Y level (4.999) is far above 2022-01 (0.876) and 2022-09 (3.572), so this is not an early-cycle sub-1% start. Versus 2022-09: today's backdrop has a live energy shock, a just-completed Fed hike, a BoJ hike to a 31-year high, and an AU inflation dashboard score of 82 — more global hawkish pressure than a UK-gilt-adjacent pause. Versus 2025-12: the 16 Sep 2026 housing print and Sep sentiment crash were not in that analog. Hard July CPI (headline 3.5%, trimmed mean 3.6%) is cooler than the retained 82 score implies, which is a regime difference versus analogs where inflation was still accelerating. Packet does not document a 2023-style banking-stress analog for Australia.

independent_checks: Policy-path versus housing/labor hard data: AONIA still +51bp by Mar-27 and +59.5bp by mid-2027 while NSW stamp-duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, employment -15.8k, unemployment 4.5% from 4.4%, and Sep consumer sentiment -5.2% to 84.4.

Cross-market rates: AU-US 2Y already -12.5bp 1d and -53.5bp 6m as local AU duration starts to outperform a still-hot US (labor score 75, activity 69, SOFR path +34.75bp by Dec-26 and +75bp by Aug-28). CA is the weaker-labor control (score 38, employment -42k, CORRA only +29bp by Dec) and CA-AU 2Y is already -165bp (10.5th percentile 5y), showing Australia as the expensive, still-hawkish housing cycle versus a labor-soft Canada.

Temperature decomposition versus retained scores: AU inflation score 82 is a dashboard_v8 headline, but July hard inputs show headline CPI easing to 3.5% and trimmed mean unchanged at 3.6%; activity 54 and consumer 48 with a fresh -4 sentiment impulse contradict the idea that the real economy can absorb +51-60bp more.

Spot cross-check, not the trade: AUDUSD still 76th percentile 1y and AUDCAD/AUDNZD at 99.8th percentile 1y show FX has not fully expressed the housing break, which is why rates (where 51-60bp remains explicitly priced) is the cleaner ownership.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: KNOWN: AU inflation remains above comfort (dashboard inflation score 82; July trimmed-mean CPI 3.6% y/y unchanged; headline CPI 3.5% after 3.8%). KNOWN: a global tightening wave (Fed hike already >90% priced into the 16 Sep decision, BoJ to 1.25%, BoE 6-3 hold with three hike votes, desk thesis that energy keeps term-rate pressure elevated even where growth is softer). NEW / newly transmitting: 16 Sep housing evidence that the RBA channel is biting now (stamp-duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, prices >7% off peak); September Westpac-MI sentiment -5.2% to 84.4 (impulse -4, clearly weaker); July employment -15.8k and unemployment 4.5% from 4.4%; 18 Sep desk note that global tightening is broadening after the Fed, which raises the odds of over-tightening into that housing break. A known tightening cycle needs this new housing/sentiment transmission to explain why AU front-end duration should be received now rather than paid.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that the residual 51-60bp AONIA hike path can be delivered, or held, once housing turnover, collateral and labor have already turned. The priced assumption treats inflation-score 82 and global tightening as dominant and housing as a side-effect the RBA will look through. The bear view is that housing is the binding constraint and that extra tightening is a policy error that gets aborted.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: ASX AONIA pricing requires the RBA to deliver roughly one 25bp hike by October (4.565), almost 40bp by year-end (4.725), 51bp by Mar-27 (4.86) and a peak near 4.945 by Jul-Sep 2027, with no material easing into early 2028. AU 2Y at 4.999 (65bp over AONIA; 99.0th percentile 1y) requires that path to stick despite housing. The 18 Sep desk thesis states the same assumption in words: energy constrains the global easing impulse and keeps term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer.

policy_path_check.rationale: Short-end AU duration requires the live AONIA/ASX path before reading AU 2Y 4.999 or AU-US 2Y +25.9bp. The US and CA paths are the controls: the US is still pricing a broader hike cycle from a hotter labor/activity set, Canada prices far less from a weaker labor set. Australia uniquely combines a housing downturn that is already in the hard data with a 51-60bp residual hike strip.

Spot is inferior: AUDUSD is only 76th percentile 1y, short AUD fights ~50bp of AONIA-over-SOFR carry (4.35 vs 3.85), and an RBA abort can be AUD-positive on a pivot. AU 2Y 4.999 (99th percentile 1y) embeds that path. The mispricing is the sustainability of those extra 51-60bp, not the existence of a still-restrictive 4.35 AONIA.

Saudi workaround reducing the extreme oil-supply tail could ease energy CPI and, perversely, let the RBA hike on domestic inflation rather than pause.
AU 2Y analog majority after a ~39bp 1m rise was further selloff, not a rally; 2022-09-28 is one episode, not a base rate.

trade.thesis: FACT: housing turnover and values are already falling under higher Australian rates, labor is loosening, and September consumer sentiment has cracked, yet AONIA still prices 51-60bp of additional tightening into 2027. INFERENCE: that residual path is a late-cycle policy error; when it is marked down, AU 2Y rallies. This is defensive duration owned where the slowdown is visible, not a mechanical short of AUD. UNKNOWN: whether energy pass-through and trimmed-mean 3.6% keep the RBA hiking through the housing break.
why_now: 16 Sep 2026 housing evidence is the new transmission of an already-known RBA tightening cycle.
18 Sep desk thesis that global tightening is broadening (Fed hike + BoJ to 1.25%) raises the policy-error odds into that housing downturn rather than validating more AU hikes.
September Westpac-MI sentiment -5.2% to 84.4 is a fresh clearly-weaker consumer impulse against July spending that was still +1.1% m/m.
AU-US 2Y already -12.5bp 1d shows the local duration bid starting; waiting for a full AUDUSD crash surrenders the rates expression where the path is explicit.
Empty $100m book still pays 5% ACT/365 vig while flat; a defined-invalidation duration long is required to have a chance of covering that hurdle.
